concepts.def: How notes start and join — legato, staccato, marcato.
Smooth and connected — notes flow together.
Short and detached — note plus a dot above.
Strongly accented — emphatic stress on a note.
How a piece is organised into sections.
Major, minor, modal, atonal — the harmonic identity.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Legato — slurred notes, no gap between them — sings. Staccato — short detached notes — bounces. Marcato — strongly accented — punches.

Accent marks (>) add weight to specific notes. Tenuto (-) means hold the note fully. Articulation transforms identical pitches into completely different musical characters.

walkthroughs.h2: Binary, ternary, rondo, strophic and more
walkthroughs.body_html:
Common structures: binary (AB), ternary (ABA), rondo (ABACA), verse-chorus, through-composed (no repeats), strophic (same music, different verses), theme & variations.

In your answers, name the structure and back it up with where each section starts.

Beyond major/minor, listen for modal tonality (Dorian, Mixolydian — folk and Celtic music), chromatic harmony (rich Romantic colour) and atonal music (no key centre — Schoenberg).

Modulation is a temporary change of key; tonality often shifts mid-piece to add interest.
